speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Thank you very much, Chris. And thanks to UNLV for hosting us.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton, thank you.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, first of all, it’s great to be with you, and thank you, everybody. The Supreme Court: It’s what it’s all about. Our country is so, so—it’s just so imperative that we have the right justices.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. Trump, thank you.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, first of all, I support the Second Amendment. I lived in Arkansas for 18 wonderful years. I represented upstate New York. I understand and respect the tradition of gun ownership. It goes back to the founding of our country.

speaker: Moderator
text: Let me bring Mr. Trump in here. The bipartisan Open Debate Coalition got millions of votes on questions to ask here, and this was, in fact, one of the top questions that they got. How will you ensure the Second Amendment is protected? You just heard Secretary Clinton’s answer. Does she persuade you that, while you may disagree on regulation, that, in fact, she supports a Second Amendment right to bear arms?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, the D.C. vs. Heller decision was very strongly—and she was extremely angry about it. I watched. I mean, she was very, very angry when upheld. And Justice Scalia was so involved. And it was a well-crafted decision. But Hillary was extremely upset, extremely angry. And people that believe in the Second Amendment and believe in it very strongly were very upset with what she had to say.

speaker: Moderator
text: Well, let me bring in Secretary Clinton. Were you extremely upset?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, I was upset because, unfortunately, dozens of toddlers injure themselves, even kill people with guns, because, unfortunately, not everyone who has loaded guns in their homes takes appropriate precautions.

speaker: Moderator
text: Let me bring Mr. Trump back into this, because, in fact, you oppose any limits on assault weapons, any limits on high-capacity magazines. You support a national right to carry law. Why, sir?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, let me just tell you before we go any further. In Chicago, which has the toughest gun laws in the United States, probably you could say by far, they have more gun violence than any other city. So we have the toughest laws, and you have tremendous gun violence.

speaker: Moderator
text: Well, let’s pick up on another issue which divides you and the justices that whoever ends up winning this election appoints could have a dramatic effect there, and that’s the issue of abortion.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. Trump, you’re pro-life. But I want to ask you specifically: Do you want the court, including the justices that you will name, to overturn Roe v. Wade, which includes—in fact, states—a woman’s right to abortion?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, if that would happen, because I am pro-life, and I will be appointing pro-life judges, I would think that that will go back to the individual states.

speaker: Moderator
text: But I’m asking you specifically. Would you like to…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: If they overturned it, it will go back to the states.

speaker: Moderator
text: But what I’m asking you, sir, is, do you want to see the court overturn—you just said you want to see the court protect the Second Amendment. Do you want to see the court overturn Roe v. Wade?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, if we put another two or perhaps three justices on, that’s really what’s going to be—that will happen. And that’ll happen automatically, in my opinion, because I am putting pro-life justices on the court. I will say this: It will go back to the states, and the states will then make a determination.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, I strongly support Roe v. Wade, which guarantees a constitutional right to a woman to make the most intimate, most difficult, in many cases, decisions about her health care that one can imagine. And in this case, it’s not only about Roe v. Wade. It is about what’s happening right now in America.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton…

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: And we have come too far to have that turned back now. And, indeed, he said women should be punished, that there should be some form of punishment for women who obtain abortions. And I could just not be more opposed to that kind of thinking.

speaker: Moderator
text: I’m going to give you a chance to respond, but I want to ask you, Secretary Clinton, I want to explore how far you believe the right to abortion goes. You have been quoted as saying that the fetus has no constitutional rights. You also voted against a ban on late-term, partial-birth abortions. Why?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Because Roe v. Wade very clearly sets out that there can be regulations on abortion so long as the life and the health of the mother are taken into account. And when I voted as a senator, I did not think that that was the case.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. Trump, your reaction? And particularly on this issue of late-term, partial-birth abortions.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, I think it’s terrible. If you go with what Hillary is saying, in the ninth month, you can take the baby and rip the baby out of the womb of the mother just prior to the birth of the baby.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, that is not what happens in these cases. And using that kind of scare rhetoric is just terribly unfortunate. You should meet with some of the women that I have met with, women I have known over the course of my life. This is one of the worst possible choices that any woman and her family has to make. And I do not believe the government should be making it.

speaker: Moderator
text: All right. But just briefly, I want to move on to another segment…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: And, honestly, nobody has business doing what I just said, doing that, as late as one or two or three or four days prior to birth. Nobody has that.

speaker: Moderator
text: All right. Let’s move on to the subject of immigration. And there is almost no issue that separates the two of you more than the issue of immigration. Actually, there are a lot of issues that separate the two of you.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, first of all, she wants to give amnesty, which is a disaster and very unfair to all of the people that are waiting in line for many, many years. We need strong borders.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. Trump, thank you. Same question to you, Secretary Clinton. Basically, why are you right and Mr. Trump is wrong?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, as he was talking, I was thinking about a young girl I met here in Las Vegas, Carla, who is very worried that her parents might be deported, because she was born in this country but they were not. They work hard, they do everything they can to give her a good life.

speaker: Moderator
text: Thank you, Secretary Clinton. I want to follow up…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Chris, I think it’s…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I think I should respond to that. First of all, I had a very good meeting with the president of Mexico. Very nice man. We will be doing very much better with Mexico on trade deals. Believe me. The NAFTA deal signed by her husband is one of the worst deals ever made of any kind, signed by anybody. It’s a disaster.

speaker: Moderator
text: Well, let me—wait, wait, sir, let me…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: We are a country of laws. We either have—and by the way…

speaker: Moderator
text: Now, wait. I’d like to hear from…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well—well, but she said one thing.

speaker: Moderator
text: I’d like to hear—I’d like to hear from Secretary Clinton.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: I voted for border security, and there are…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: And the wall.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: There are some limited places where that was appropriate. There also is necessarily going to be new technology and how best to deploy that.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. Trump?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: President Obama has moved millions of people out. Nobody knows about it, nobody talks about it. But under Obama, millions of people have been moved out of this country. They’ve been deported. She doesn’t want to say that, but that’s what’s happened, and that’s what happened big league.

speaker: Moderator
text: I want to…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: But what she doesn’t say is that President Obama has deported millions and millions of people just the way it is.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton, I want to…

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: We will not have open borders. That is…

speaker: Moderator
text: Well, let me—Secretary…

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: That is a rank mischaracterization.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton…

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: We will have secure borders, but we’ll also have reform. And this used to be a bipartisan issue. Ronald Reagan was the last president…

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton, excuse me. Secretary Clinton.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … to sign immigration reform, and George W. Bush supported it, as well.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton, I want to clear up your position on this issue, because in a speech you gave to a Brazilian bank, for which you were paid $225,000, we’ve learned from the WikiLeaks, that you said this, and I want to quote. “My dream is a hemispheric common market with open trade and open borders.” So that’s the question…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Thank you.

speaker: Moderator
text: That’s the question. Please quiet, everybody. Is that your dream, open borders?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, if you went on to read the rest of the sentence, I was talking about energy. You know, we trade more energy with our neighbors than we trade with the rest of the world combined. And I do want us to have an electric grid, an energy system that crosses borders. I think that would be a great benefit to us.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: That was a great pivot off the fact that she wants open borders, OK? How did we get on to Putin?

speaker: Moderator
text: Hold on—hold on, wait. Hold on, folks. Because we—this is going to end up getting out of control. Let’s try to keep it quiet so—for the candidates and for the American people.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: So just to finish on the borders…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: She wants open borders. People are going to pour into our country. People are going to come in from Syria. She wants 550 percent more people than Barack Obama, and he has thousands and thousands of people. They have no idea where they come from.

speaker: Moderator
text: Wait, but…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: … from everything I see, has no respect for this person.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, that’s because he’d rather have a puppet as president of the United States.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: No puppet. No puppet.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: And it’s pretty clear…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: You’re the puppet!

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: It’s pretty clear you won’t admit…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: No, you’re the puppet.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … that the Russians have engaged in cyberattacks against the United States of America, that you encouraged espionage against our people, that you are willing to spout the Putin line, sign up for his wish list, break up NATO, do whatever he wants to do, and that you continue to get help from him, because he has a very clear favorite in this race.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton…

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: And I think it’s time you take a stand…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: She has no idea whether it’s Russia, China, or anybody else.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: I am not quoting myself.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: She has no idea.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: I am quoting 17…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Hillary, you have no idea.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … 17 intelligence—do you doubt 17 military and civilian…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: And our country has no idea.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … agencies.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Yeah, I doubt it. I doubt it.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, he’d rather believe Vladimir Putin than the military and civilian intelligence professionals who are sworn to protect us. I find that just absolutely…[crosstalk]

speaker: Donald Trump
text: She doesn’t like Putin because Putin has outsmarted her at every step of the way.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. Trump…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Excuse me. Putin has outsmarted her in Syria.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. Trump…[crosstalk]

speaker: Donald Trump
text: He’s outsmarted her every step of the way.

speaker: Moderator
text: I’m not a potted plant here, I do get to ask some questions.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Yes, that’s fine.

speaker: Moderator
text: And I would like to ask you this direct question. The top national security officials of this country do believe that Russia has been behind these hacks. Even if you don’t know for sure whether they are, do you condemn any interference by Russia in the American election?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: By Russia or anybody else.

speaker: Moderator
text: You condemn their interference?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Of course I condemn. Of course I—I don’t know Putin. I have no idea.

speaker: Moderator
text: I’m not asking—I’m asking do you condemn?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I never met Putin. This is not my best friend. But if the United States got along with Russia, wouldn’t be so bad.

speaker: Moderator
text: We’re a long way away from immigration, but I’m going to let you finish this topic. You got about 45 seconds.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: And she always will be.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: I—I find it ironic that he’s raising nuclear weapons. This is a person who has been very cavalier, even casual about the use of nuclear weapons. He’s…

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … advocated more countries getting them, Japan, Korea, even Saudi Arabia. He said, well, if we have them, why don’t we use them, which I think is terrifying.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I have 200 generals…

speaker: Moderator
text: Very quickly.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: … and admirals, 21 endorsing me, 21 congressional Medal of Honor recipients. As far as Japan and other countries, we are being ripped off by everybody in the—we’re defending other countries. We are spending a fortune doing it. They have the bargain of the century.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Look, she’s been proven to be a liar on so many different ways. This is just another lie.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, I’m just quoting you when you were asked…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: There’s no quote. You’re not going to find a quote from me.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … about a potential nuclear—nuclear competition in Asia, you said, you know, go ahead, enjoy yourselves, folks. That kind…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: And defend yourselves.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … of language—well…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: And defend yourselves. I didn’t say nuclear. And defend yourself.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: The United States has kept the peace—the United States has kept the peace through our alliances. Donald wants to tear up our alliances. I think it makes the world safer and, frankly, it makes the United States safer. I would work with our allies in Asia, in Europe, in the Middle East, and elsewhere. That’s the only way we’re going to be able to keep the peace.

speaker: Moderator
text: We’re going to—no, we are going to move on to the next topic, which is the economy. And I hope we handle that as well as we did immigration. You also have very different ideas about how to get the economy growing faster. Secretary Clinton, in your plan, government plays a big role. You see more government spending, more entitlements, more tax credits, more tax penalties. Mr. Trump, you want to get government out with lower taxes and less regulation.

speaker: Moderator
text: We’re going to drill down into this a little bit more. But in this overview, please explain to me why you believe that your plan will create more jobs and growth for this country and your opponent’s plan will not. In this round, you go first, Secretary Clinton.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, I think when the middle class thrives, America thrives. And so my plan is based on growing the economy, giving middle-class families many more opportunities. I want us to have the biggest jobs program since World War II, jobs in infrastructure and advanced manufacturing. I think we can compete with high-wage countries, and I believe we should. New jobs and clean energy, not only to fight climate change, which is a serious problem, but to create new opportunities and new businesses.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary, thank you. Mr. Trump, why will your plan create more jobs and growth than Secretary Clinton’s?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, first of all, before I start on my plan, her plan is going to raise taxes and even double your taxes. Her tax plan is a disaster. And she can say all she wants about college tuition. And I’m a big proponent. We’re going to do a lot of things for college tuition. But the rest of the public’s going to be paying for it. We will have a massive, massive tax increase under Hillary Clinton’s plan.

speaker: Moderator
text: Time, Mr. Trump.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: … that’s offshore back into the country. We are going to start the engine rolling again, because…

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. Trump?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: … right now, our country is dying at 1 percent GDP.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, let me translate that, if I can, Chris, because…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: You can’t.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … the fact is, he’s going to advocate for the largest tax cuts we’ve ever seen, three times more than the tax cuts under the Bush administration. I have said repeatedly throughout this campaign: I will not raise taxes on anyone making $250,000 or less.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary…

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Cutting taxes on the wealthy, we’ve tried that. It has not worked the way that it has been promised.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton, I want to pursue your plan, because in many ways it is similar to the Obama stimulus plan in 2009, which has led to the slowest GDP growth since 1949.

speaker: Moderator
text: Thank you, sir.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, it’s a combination, Chris. And let me say that when you inherit the level of economic catastrophe that President Obama inherited, it was a real touch-and-go situation. I was in the Senate before I became secretary of state. I’ve never seen people as physically distraught as the Bush administration team was because of what was happening to the economy.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. Trump, even conservative economists who have looked at your plan say that the numbers don’t add up, that your idea, and you’ve talked about 25 million jobs created, 4 percent…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Over a 10-year period.

speaker: Moderator
text: … growth is unrealistic. And they say—you talk a lot about growing the energy industry. They say with oil prices as low as they are right now, that’s unrealistic, as well. Your response, sir?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: So I just left some high representatives of India. They’re growing at 8 percent. China is growing at 7 percent. And that for them is a catastrophically low number.

speaker: Moderator
text: I want you to give you a chance to briefly speak to that, and then I want to pivot to one-sixth of the economy…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: And that will be as bad as NAFTA.

speaker: Moderator
text: … which is Obamacare. But go ahead, briefly.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, first, let me say, number one, when I saw the final agreement for TPP, I said I was against it. It didn’t meet my test. I’ve had the same test. Does it create jobs, raise incomes, and further our national security? I’m against it now. I’ll be against it after the election. I’ll be against it when I’m president.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. Trump?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: That’s the kind of approach that is just not going to work.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, let me just say—let me just say.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: We’re going to pull the country together. We’re going to have trade agreements that we enforce. That’s why I’m going to have a trade prosecutor for the first time in history. And we’re going to enforce those agreements, and we’re going to look for businesses to help us by buying American products.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton? Go ahead, Mr. Trump.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I ask a simple question. She’s been doing this for 30 years. Why the hell didn’t you do it over the last 15, 20 years?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: No, I voted.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: You were very much involved—excuse me. My turn. You were very much involved in every aspect of this country. Very much. And you do have experience. I say the one thing you have over me is experience, but it’s bad experience, because what you’ve done has turned out badly.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, first of all, what he just said about the State Department is not only untrue, it’s been debunked numerous times.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Give me a break.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: And on the day when I was in the Situation Room, monitoring the raid that brought Osama bin Laden to justice, he was hosting the “Celebrity Apprentice.” So I’m happy to compare my 30 years of experience, what I’ve done for this country, trying to help in every way I could, especially kids and families get ahead and stay ahead, with your 30 years, and I’ll let the American people make that decision.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, I think I did a much better job. I built a massive company, a great company, some of the greatest assets anywhere in the world, worth many, many billions of dollars. I started with a $1 million loan. I agree with that. It’s a $1 million loan. But I built a phenomenal company.

speaker: Moderator
text: All right. We are going to get to foreign hot spots in a few moments, but the next segment is fitness to be president of the United States. Mr. Trump, at the last debate, you said your talk about grabbing women was just that, talk, and that you’d never actually done it. And since then, as we all know, nine women have come forward and said that you either groped them or kissed them without their consent.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, first of all, those stories have been largely debunked. Those people—I don’t know those people. I have a feeling how they came. I believe it was her campaign that did it.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: At the last debate, we heard Donald talking about what he did to women. And after that, a number of women have come forward saying that’s exactly what he did to them. Now, what was his response? Well, he held a number of big rallies where he said that he could not possibly have done those things to those women because they were not attractive enough for them to be assaulted.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I did not say that. I did not say that.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: In fact, he went on to say…

speaker: Moderator
text: Her two minutes—sir, her two minutes. Her two minutes.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I did not say that.

speaker: Moderator
text: It’s her two minutes.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: He went on to say, “Look at her. I don’t think so.” About another woman, he said, “That wouldn’t be my first choice.” He attacked the woman reporter writing the story, called her “disgusting,” as he has called a number of women during this campaign.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. Trump…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Nobody has more respect for women than I do. Nobody. [laughter]

speaker: Moderator
text: Please, everybody.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: And frankly, those stories have been largely debunked. And I really want to just talk about something slightly different.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, every time Donald is pushed on something which is obviously uncomfortable, like what these women are saying, he immediately goes to denying responsibility. And it’s not just about women. He never apologizes or says he’s sorry for anything.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: He went after Mr. and Mrs. Khan, the parents of a young man who died serving our country, a Gold Star family, because of their religion. speaker: Donald Trump
text: So sad when she talks about violence at my rallies, and she caused the violence. It’s on tape.

speaker: Moderator
text: During the last…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: The other things are false, but honestly, I’d love to talk about getting rid of ISIS, and I’d love to talk about other things…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: … but those other charges, as she knows, are false.

speaker: Moderator
text: In this bucket about fitness to be president, there’s been a lot of developments over the last 10 days since the last debate. I’d like to ask you about them. These are questions that the American people have.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, everything I did as secretary of state was in furtherance of our country’s interests and our values. The State Department has said that. I think that’s been proven.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton…

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … we have made environments in schools healthier for kids, including healthier lunches…

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton, respectfully, this is—this is an open discussion.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, it is an open discussion. And you…

speaker: Moderator
text: And the specific question went to pay for play. Do you want to talk about that?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, but there is no—but there is no evidence—but there is…[crosstalk]

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I think that it’s been very well…

speaker: Moderator
text: Let’s ask Mr. Trump.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: There is a lot of evidence about the very good work…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: It’s been very well studied.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … and the high rankings…[crosstalk]

speaker: Moderator
text: Please let Mr. Trump speak.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: … and it’s a criminal enterprise, and so many people know it.

speaker: Moderator
text: Please let Mr. Trump speak.

text: It’s a criminal enterprise. Saudi Arabia giving $25 million, Qatar, all of these countries. You talk about women and women’s rights? So these are people that push gays off business—off buildings. These are people that kill women and treat women horribly. And yet you take their money.

text: Secretary Clinton?

text: Well, very quickly, we at the Clinton Foundation spend 90 percent—90 percent of all the money that is donated on behalf of programs of people around the world and in our own country. speaker: Moderator
text: All right.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … because it’s an important part of the American experience.

text: They don’t want you to help them anymore.

text: I’d like to mention one thing. Trump Foundation, small foundation. People contribute, I contribute. text: Wasn’t some of the money used to settle your lawsuits, sir?

text: No, it was—we put up the American flag. And that’s it. They put up the American flag. We fought for the right in Palm Beach to put up the American flag.

text: Right. But there was a penalty that was imposed by Palm Beach County, and the money came from your foundation…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: There was. There was. And, by the way…

speaker: Moderator
text: … instead of Mar-a-Lago or yourself, sir.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: … the money—the money went to Fisher House, where they build houses—the money that you’re talking about went to Fisher House, where they build houses for veterans and disabled vets.

speaker: Moderator
text: I want to get into one…

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: But, of course, there’s no way we can know whether any of that is true, because he hasn’t released his tax returns. You can look at our tax returns. We’ve got them all out there.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: So let me just tell you very quickly, we’re entitled because of the laws that people like her passed to take massive amounts of depreciation on other charges, and we do it. And all of her donors—just about all of them—I know Buffett took hundreds of millions of dollars, Soros, George Soros, took hundreds of millions of dollars…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Let me just explain.

speaker: Moderator
text: But, no, we heard this…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Most of her donors have done the same thing as I do.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. Trump, we—OK.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: You know what she should have done?

speaker: Moderator
text: Folks, we heard this…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: And you know, Hillary, what you should have done, you should have changed the law when you were a United States senator…

speaker: Moderator
text: Folks, we heard this…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: … because your donors and your special interests are doing the same thing as I do, except even more so.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, you know…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: You should have changed the law. But you won’t change the law, because you take in so much money. I mean, I sat in my apartment today on a very beautiful hotel down the street known as Trump…

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Made with Chinese steel.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: But I will tell you, I sat there…[laughter]… I sat there watching ad after ad after ad, false ad. All paid for by your friends on Wall Street that gave so much money because they know you’re going to protect them. And, frankly, you should have changed the laws.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. Trump…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: If you don’t like what I did, you should have changed the laws.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. Trump, I want to ask you about one last question in this topic. You have been warning at rallies recently that this election is rigged and that Hillary Clinton is in the process of trying to steal it from you.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I will look at it at the time. I’m not looking at anything now. I’ll look at it at the time.

speaker: Moderator
text: But, sir, there’s…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: If you look—excuse me, Chris—if you look at your voter rolls, you will see millions of people that are registered to vote—millions, this isn’t coming from me—this is coming from Pew Report and other places—millions of people that are registered to vote that shouldn’t be registered to vote.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Chris, she should never have been allowed to run for the presidency based on what she did with e-mails and so many other things.

speaker: Moderator
text: But, sir, there is a tradition in this country—in fact, one of the prides of this country—is the peaceful transition of power and that no matter how hard-fought a campaign is, that at the end of the campaign that the loser concedes to the winner. Not saying that you’re necessarily going to be the loser or the winner, but that the loser concedes to the winner and that the country comes together in part for the good of the country. Are you saying you’re not prepared now to commit to that principle?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: What I’m saying is that I will tell you at the time. I’ll keep you in suspense. OK?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, Chris, let me respond to that, because that’s horrifying. You know, every time Donald thinks things are not going in his direction, he claims whatever it is, is rigged against him.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Should have gotten it. [laughter]

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: This is—this is a mindset. This is how Donald thinks. And it’s funny, but it’s also really troubling.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: So that is not the way our democracy works. We’ve been around for 240 years. We’ve had free and fair elections. We’ve accepted the outcomes when we may not have liked them. And that is what must be expected of anyone standing on a debate stage during a general election. You know, President Obama said the other day when you’re whining before the game is even finished… [applause]

speaker: Moderator
text: Hold on. Hold on, folks. Hold on, folks.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … it just shows you’re not up to doing the job. And let’s—you know, let’s be clear about what he is saying and what that means. He is denigrating—he’s talking down our democracy. And I, for one, am appalled that somebody who is the nominee of one of our two major parties would take that kind of position.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I think what the FBI did and what the Department of Justice did, including meeting with her husband, the attorney general, in the back of an airplane on the tarmac in Arizona, I think it’s disgraceful. I think it’s a disgrace.

speaker: Moderator
text: All right.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I think we’ve never had a situation so bad in this country. [applause]

speaker: Moderator
text: Hold on, folks. This doesn’t do any good for anyone. Let’s please continue the debate, and let’s move on to the subject of foreign hot spots.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, I am encouraged that there is an effort led by the Iraqi army, supported by Kurdish forces, and also given the help and advice from the number of special forces and other Americans on the ground. But I will not support putting American soldiers into Iraq as an occupying force. I don’t think that is in our interest, and I don’t think that would be smart to do. In fact, Chris, I think that would be a big red flag waving for ISIS to reconstitute itself.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. Trump, same question. If we are able to push ISIS out of Mosul and out of Iraq, will—would you be willing to put U.S. troops in there to prevent their return or something else?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Let me tell you, Mosul is so sad. We had Mosul. But when she left, when she took everybody out, we lost Mosul. Now we’re fighting again to get Mosul. The problem with Mosul and what they wanted to do is they wanted to get the leaders of ISIS who they felt were in Mosul.

speaker: Moderator
text: Sir, your two minutes are up.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: The point is, the big winner is going to be Iran.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, you know, once again, Donald is implying that he didn’t support the invasion of Iraq. I said it was a mistake. I’ve said that years ago. He has consistently denied what is…

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … a very clear fact that…

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … before the invasion, he supported it. And, you know, I just want everybody to go Google it. Google “Donald Trump Iraq.” And you will see the dozens of sources which verify that he was for the invasion of Iraq.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: And you can actually hear the audio of him saying that. Now, why does that matter? Well, it matters because he has not told the truth about that position. I guess he believes it makes him look better now to contrast with me because I did vote for it.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Chris, we don’t gain anything.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: He has all the conspiracy theories…[crosstalk]

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Iran is taking over Iraq.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton, it’s…[crosstalk]

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Iran is taking over Iraq. We don’t gain anything.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: This conspiracy theory, which he’s been spewing out for quite some time.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: We would’ve gained if they did it by surprise…[crosstalk]

speaker: Moderator
text: Wait, wait, wait, Secretary Clinton, it’s an open discussion.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: He says…[crosstalk]

speaker: Donald Trump
text: We would have gained if they did it by surprise.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary, please let Mr. Trump speak.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … unfit, and he proves it every time he talks.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: No, you are the one that’s unfit. You know, WikiLeaks just actually came out—John Podesta said some horrible things about you, and, boy, was he right. He said some beauties. And you know, Bernie Sanders, he said you have bad judgment. You do.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, you should ask Bernie Sanders who he’s supporting for president. And he has said…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Which is a big mistake.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … as he has campaigned for me around the country, you are the most dangerous person to run for president in the modern history of America. I think he’s right.

speaker: Moderator
text: Let’s turn to Aleppo. Mr. Trump, in the last debate, you were both asked about the situation in the Syrian city of Aleppo. And I want to follow up on that, because you said several things in that debate which were not true, sir. You said that Aleppo has basically fallen. In fact, there—in fact, there are…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: It’s a catastrophe. I mean…

speaker: Moderator
text: It’s a catastrophe, but there…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: … it’s a mess.

speaker: Moderator
text: There are a quarter of…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Have you seen it? Have you seen it?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Have you seen what’s happened to Aleppo?

speaker: Moderator
text: Sir, if I may finish my question…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: OK, so it hasn’t fallen. Take a look at it.

speaker: Moderator
text: Well, there are a quarter of a million people still living there and being slaughtered.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: That’s right. And they are being slaughtered…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: … because of bad decisions.

speaker: Moderator
text: If I may just finish here, and you also said that—that Syria and Russia are busy fighting ISIS. In fact, they have been the ones who’ve been bombing and shelling eastern Aleppo, and they just announced a humanitarian pause, in effect, admitting that they have been bombing and shelling Aleppo. Would you like to clear that up, sir?

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, Aleppo is a disaster. It’s a humanitarian nightmare. But it has fallen from the—from any standpoint. I mean, what do you need, a signed document? Take a look at Aleppo. It is so sad when you see what’s happened.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: … in many cases, ISIS-aligned, and we now have them in our country, and wait until you see—this is going to be the great Trojan horse. And wait until you see what happens in the coming years. Lots of luck, Hillary. Thanks a lot for doing a great job.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton, you have talked about—and in the last debate and again today—that you would impose a no-fly zone to try to protect the people of Aleppo and to stop the killing there. President Obama has refused to do that because he fears it’s going to draw us closer or deeper into the conflict.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, Chris, first of all, I think a no-fly zone could save lives and could hasten the end of the conflict. I’m well aware of the really legitimate concerns that you have expressed from both the president and the general.

speaker: Moderator
text: Folks, I want to get into our final segment.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: But I just have to…

speaker: Moderator
text: Real quick.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: It’s so ridiculous what she—she will defeat ISIS. We should have never let ISIS happen in the first place. And right now, they’re in 32 countries.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: We should have—wait one second. They had a cease-fire three weeks ago. A cease-fire, United States, Russia, and Syria. And during the cease-fire, Russia took over vast swatches of land, and then they said we don’t want the cease-fire anymore.

speaker: Moderator
text: Mr. Trump, Secretary Clinton—no, we need to move on to our final segment, and that is the national debt, which has not been discussed until tonight.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Well, I say they’re wrong, because I’m going to create tremendous jobs. And we’re bringing GDP from, really, 1 percent, which is what it is now, and if she got in, it will be less than zero. But we’re bringing it from 1 percent up to 4 percent. And I actually think we can go higher than 4 percent. I think you can go to 5 percent or 6 percent. And if we do, you don’t have to bother asking your question, because we have a tremendous machine. We will have created a tremendous economic machine once again. To do that, we’re taking back jobs. We’re not going to let our companies be raided by other countries where we lose all our jobs, we don’t make our product anymore. It’s very sad. But I’m going to create a—the kind of a country that we were from the standpoint of industry. We used to be there. We’ve given it up. We’ve become very, very sloppy.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, first, when I hear Donald talk like that and know that his slogan is “Make America Great Again,” I wonder when he thought America was great. And before he rushes and says, “You know, before you and President Obama were there,” I think it’s important to recognize that he has been criticizing our government for decades.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Yeah, yeah, we’ve heard—we’ve heard this before, Hillary.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: I started off with—my dad was a small-business man.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: We’ve heard this before.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: And I think it—you know, it’s a difference that affects how we see the world and what we want to do with the economy.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Thank you, Hillary. Could I just respond?

speaker: Moderator
text: Well, no, sir, because we’re running out of time…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Because I did disagree with Ronald Reagan very strongly on trade. I disagreed with him. We should have been much tougher on trade even then. I’ve been waiting for years. Nobody does it right.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: And frankly, now we’re going to do it right.

speaker: Moderator
text: All right. The one last area I want to get into with you in this debate is the fact that the biggest driver of our debt is entitlements, which is 60 percent of all federal spending. Now, the Committee for federal—a Responsible Federal Budget has looked at both of your plans and they say neither of you has a serious plan that is going to solve the fact that Medicare’s going to run out of money in the 2020s, Social Security is going to run out of money in the 2030s, and at that time, recipients are going to take huge cuts in their benefits.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: I’m cutting taxes. We’re going to grow the economy. It’s going to grow at a record rate of growth.

speaker: Moderator
text: That’s not going to help in the entitlements.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: No, it’s going to totally help you. And one thing we have to do: Repeal and replace the disaster known as Obamacare. It’s destroying our country. It’s destroying our businesses, our small business and our big businesses. We have to repeal and replace Obamacare.

speaker: Moderator
text: And, Secretary Clinton, same question, because at this point, Social Security and Medicare are going to run out, the trust funds are going to run out of money. Will you as president entertain—will you consider a grand bargain, a deal that includes both tax increases and benefit cuts to try to save both programs?

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, Chris, I am on record as saying that we need to put more money into the Social Security Trust Fund. That’s part of my commitment to raise taxes on the wealthy. My Social Security payroll contribution will go up, as will Donald’s, assuming he can’t figure out how to get out of it. But what we want to do is to replenish the Social Security Trust Fund…

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Such a nasty woman.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … by making sure that we have sufficient resources, and that will come from either raising the cap and/or finding other ways to get more money into it. I will not cut benefits. I want to enhance benefits for low-income workers and for women who have been disadvantaged by the current Social Security system.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: Your husband disagrees with you.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: … the long-term health care drivers. We’ve got to get costs down, increase value, emphasize wellness. I have a plan for doing that. And I think that we will be able to get entitlement spending under control by with more resources and smarter decisions.

speaker: Moderator
text: This is—this is the final time, probably to both of your delight, that you’re going to be on a stage together in this campaign. I would like to end it on a positive note. You had not agreed to closing statements, but it seems to me in a funny way that might make it more interesting because you haven’t prepared closing statements.

speaker: Bill Clinton
text: Well, I would like to say to everyone watching tonight that I’m reaching out to all Americans—Democrats, Republicans, and independents—because we need everybody to help make our country what it should be, to grow the economy, to make it fairer, to make it work for everyone. We need your talents, your skills, your commitments, your energy, your ambition.

speaker: Moderator
text: Secretary Clinton, thank you.

speaker: Donald Trump
text: She’s raising the money from the people she wants to control. Doesn’t work that way.

speaker: Moderator
text: Thank you both. [applause]
